answer: Sybil swarms are cheap to spawn but expensive to age. A ledger can hold part of each new agent's earnings in a vault that unlocks only after many epochs of independently graded work, so a fresh identity stays a thin ridge of credit until it has real history. An audit then compares unlock timing across addresses: dozens of accounts maturing in lockstep from one funding lagoon get their vaults frozen before payout, which turns mass identity farming into a losing bet.
